title: Your Phone System Is About to Cost You More (Here's Why)
excerpt: Hardware shortages are pushing up prices across the board, and your business phone setup is next on the list.

content.text: Okay, so this isn't breaking news exactly, but it's the kind of thing that'll sneak up on you if you're not paying attention. Memory shortages—the stuff that powers basically everything in tech—are getting worse, and that ripple effect is hitting businesses in their wallets. We're seeing component prices jump 20-30% in some cases, and honestly, phone systems are right in the crosshairs.

There's a global shortage of memory chips (RAM and storage), and manufacturers are dealing with supply chain chaos. Electronics makers are passing those costs straight to consumers. We've already seen it with MacBooks shipping late and gaming hardware getting ridiculously expensive. Phone system providers? They're next. Whether you're looking at cloud-based VoIP or on-premise hardware, the components they use are getting pricier.

items: Equipment costs for on-premise systems are climbing
Providers might start building price increases into their service tiers
If you've been putting off a phone system upgrade, the window to lock in better pricing is closing

content.text: Memory chip prices are up 20-30% in some markets. If you need new equipment, waiting could mean paying significantly more in a few months.

If you're running an older phone system and thinking about upgrading, or if you're shopping around for a new provider, now is the time to move. Not six months from now. Not next quarter. Here's the thing—phone systems are already a line item most small business owners don't love spending on. Adding 20-30% to that bill? That stings.

content.label: Intecha's Take
content.text: Get quotes NOW if you've been considering a switch or upgrade. Lock in pricing with a vendor before they adjust their rates. If you're on a cloud-based VoIP system, you're actually in a better spot because you're not buying hardware—but definitely lock in your contract terms while they're still reasonable. And if you've got an aging on-premise system? This is your sign. Cloud-based options are looking better every day, and the cost difference just got smaller.

The broader lesson here: don't wait on tech decisions thinking prices will come down. They're not. Get in front of this, talk to your provider about what's coming, and make your moves while you still can. Your budget will thank you.
